ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a tetrahedral center, and the central carbon is connected to the negatively charged oxygen O− above, OR3 on the left, R2 on the upper left, and the adjacent carbon on the right. The adjacent carbon is also connected to an R substituent and is connected to the ester group C(=O)OR1 on the right. The curved arrow in the figure shows that the electrons of the upper O− return to the left tetrahedral center to form a carbonyl group, while another curved arrow shows that the electrons of the C−OR3 bond transfer to OR3, causing OR3 to leave. Reasoning: After arrow pushing, the left tetrahedral center collapses into a carbonyl C=O and retains its R2 substituent and the connection to the middle carbon; OR3 is expelled as the leaving group. The middle carbon still bears an R substituent, and the right ester group C(=O)OR1 remains unchanged. Using the wildcard [*] to represent the R/R1/R2 type generic substituents in the figure, the product skeleton corresponds to the SMILES O=C(C([*])C(O[*])=O)O[*].

method.method_draft: Identify the left tetrahedral center in the image. Apply the arrows: collapse the top O− into a carbonyl at that left center and expel the OR3 group. planner_metadata.image_role: From the image, extract the atom framework: a central carbon bearing R connects to a right ester carbonyl C(=O)OR1 and to a left acyl-derived center bearing an oxygen with negative charge and an alkoxy substituent OR3; the arrows show an intramolecular re-formation of a carbonyl at that left center and loss of an alkoxy substituent.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the wording 'after the electron has been relocated' to know that only the electron-flow consequence, not a separate reagent transformation, is requested as the final molecular state.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use valence and charge conservation for a tetrahedral acyl intermediate: the negatively charged oxygen must become neutral by forming a double bond to carbon; one single bond at that carbon must be lost to avoid five valence electrons around carbon, so the alkoxy group is the leaving group. The stable product is the neutral diester/dicarbonyl skeleton with unspecified substituents represented by [*].
